purpose: Methenamine hippurate is used to prevent urinary tract infections (UTIs) from coming back, especially in people who get them often. It is not used to treat an active infection, but rather to keep new ones from starting. Your doctor may recommend it for long-term use if you keep getting UTIs.
how_it_works: When you take this medicine, it travels to your bladder and urine. Once there, the acidic environment of your urine converts it into a substance called formaldehyde, which kills the bacteria in your urine before they can multiply and cause an infection. It basically turns your urine into an unfriendly place for bacteria to grow.
common_side_effects: Nausea, upset stomach, or stomach cramps are the most common issues. Some people notice a rash or skin irritation. You may also experience a mild burning feeling when you urinate, or you might need to urinate more often than usual.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have kidney problems, liver disease, or gout, as this medicine may not be safe for you. Do not take it if you are dehydrated or if you cannot urinate well. It should not be taken with sulfonamide antibiotics (like Bactrim) because they can form a harmful combination. Drink plenty of fluids while taking this medicine. Let your doctor know if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is one tablet (1 gram) taken twice a day, once in the morning and once at night. It is best taken with food to help avoid stomach upset. Your doctor may also recommend taking vitamin C or eating certain foods to keep your urine acidic, which helps the medicine work better.
